head: d6ed165

findings.title: Stale 'TLS handshake deadline' wording after d61ce2d removed the separate handshake deadline
findings.description: d61ce2d deleted TlsConnector's own Watchdog: the handshake now runs only under the exchange's total-timeout reservation, so there are exactly two kinds of deadline (write, total). The Scheduler javadoc still opens with 'The JVM-wide scheduler of the write, total and TLS handshake deadlines', which contradicts its own last sentence. The same stale claim is in WatchdogTest (class doc line 52 'enforces the write, total and TLS handshake deadlines', line 121 'every https request its handshake deadline', line 147 'the one an https request's handshake deadline uses') and in the SRS trace link docs/spec/22.reverse-proxy.srs.md:2304 ('TLS handshake deadline armed on ProxyExchange.Scheduler'). Cost: a maintainer reading these looks for a third deadline (or re-adds one), and the REL-PROXY-002 AC-2/AC-3 test comments describe a queue load (one extra reservation per https request) that no longer exists.
findings.evidence: ProxyExchange.java:335 '* The JVM-wide scheduler of the write, total and TLS handshake deadlines, ...' vs. ProxyExchange.java:339-340 'The TLS handshake runs under the request's total-timeout reservation'; TlsConnector.layer no longer schedules anything (git show d61ce2d removes TlsConnector.Watchdog.arm).
findings.fix_hint: Say 'of the write and total deadlines (the TLS handshake runs under the total one)'; update the three WatchdogTest comments and the SRS trace-link note.
